questions.stem: The Bhakti saint who founded the Sikh religion in the 15th century was:
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak (1469-1539) founded Sikhism, emphasising one formless God (Ik Onkar), equality, and service. Kabir (1440-1518) was a Bhakti-Sufi poet whose verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib but he is not the founder of Sikhism. Ramananda (c. 14th century) preached Bhakti in the Ganga valley and was Kabir's guru. Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas.

questions.stem: The Bhakti saint Mirabai is famous for her devotion to:
questions.explanation: Mirabai (c. 1498-1547) — Rajput princess of Mewar — wrote passionate devotional songs to Krishna and left her palace to wander as a bhakta. She is part of the Nirguna-Saguna Bhakti tradition; her 'Meera Bhajans' are still sung across India. Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas) and Tyagaraja focus on Rama; Basavanna on Shiva (through the Virashaiva movement in Karnataka).

questions.stem: The most influential Sufi order in medieval India, based at the shrine of Khwaja Moinuddin at Ajmer, is the:
questions.explanation: The Chishti order was founded in India by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (d. 1236) at Ajmer. Other great Chishti saints — Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi), Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Delhi), Baba Farid (Ajodhan/Punjab), Shaikh Salim Chishti (Fatehpur Sikri). Suhrawardi order — centred in Multan. Qadri — popular in the Deccan. Naqshbandi — emphasised orthodoxy; Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi (Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani) opposed Din-i-Ilahi.

questions.stem: The Bhakti saint Ramanuja (11th-12th century) is known as the founder of:
questions.explanation: Ramanuja (1017-1137) propagated Vishishtadvaita ('qualified non-dualism') — Brahman is one but qualified by real attributes of souls and matter. Advaita (pure non-dualism) — Adi Shankaracharya (788-820). Dvaita (dualism) — Madhvacharya (13th century). Shuddhadvaita (pure non-dualism with form) — Vallabhacharya (15th-16th century). Ramanuja led the Sri Vaishnava tradition from Srirangam.

questions.stem: Sant Kabir's verses are collected in a work called:
questions.explanation: Kabir's dohas and verses are mainly preserved in the 'Bijak' (compiled by his followers). Selected verses also appear in the Guru Granth Sahib. Vinay Patrika is by Tulsidas; Sur Sagar by Surdas; Padavali is the common term for collected songs of several saints (e.g., Vidyapati's Padavali). Kabir rejected ritual, caste, idolatry, and stressed personal experience of one formless God.

questions.stem: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya — one of the greatest Chishti saints — lived during the reign of:

options.option_text: The later Khilji and early Tughlaq sultans

questions.explanation: Nizamuddin Auliya (1238-1325) lived in Delhi during the reigns of seven sultans — from Balban to Muhammad bin Tughlaq. His disciples included the poet Amir Khusrau and the Sufi Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehli. His dargah at Nizamuddin, Delhi, is a major pilgrimage site even today. Akbar (r. 1556-1605) and Shah Jahan / Aurangzeb ruled much later.

questions.stem: The Bhakti saint Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who popularised the chanting of Krishna's name in Bengal and Odisha, lived in the:
questions.explanation: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534) — founder of the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition. Popularised congregational chanting (sankirtan) of 'Hare Krishna'. Settled at Puri, Odisha. Later influenced ISKCON (the 'Hare Krishna' movement, founded 1966 by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada).
